Pick the jar that matches your game: install Fabric Loader and the Fabric API for that Minecraft version, then put the jar in the client `mods` folder. Mod Menu is optional; with Mod Menu Updater installed this mod lists updates and leaves installing to it.

## [0.3.7] - 2026-11-01

### Added

- **The install screen says what it is doing.** Under the bar it prints the jar being fetched, its
  size and the speed it arrived at, so a download that takes a minute no longer looks stuck.
- **The mod speaks its own language.** The Interface row in the settings cycles through the fifteen
  shipped languages, or back to the game language, without touching Minecraft's own language; keys
  the mod does not override still come from the game.
- Quilt loads this jar through its own Fabric compatibility, and the update check asks `quilt` first
  when the Quilt loader is present. Documented in `AGENTS.md`, not verified in game on Quilt.
- **The update list names its columns.** Mod, Installed, New and Select, so the box on the right and
  the name on the left are no longer left to guess.

### Changed

- **Mod icons are smaller and inset from the table edge.** Twelve pixels with a margin, and the name
  starts at a fixed column instead of hugging the icon.

### Fixed

- **Rescan no longer freezes the menu.** The measurement did run again, but on the render thread, so
  the game stopped for the whole walk and, because nothing had changed on disk, the numbers looked
  identical; it now runs on the mod's own worker thread and the menu says it is running while it
  does. (Corrected: this note first said the button reused the last measurement, which it did not.)
- **A build that is already installed is no longer offered under a game-version prefix.** Collective
  8.72 was offered as `26.3.0-8.72`, which is the same jar under another name.

---

## [0.3.6] - 2026-10-31

### Fixed

- **The update list shows the mod's real icon, not a blank tile.** Every icon was drawn by sampling
  only its top left corner, so a 128 pixel image came out as an empty square; each icon is now scaled
  once to the 16 pixel size a row draws it at.
- **A row is no longer offered for a file that has no version number.** A mirror that publishes
  `<26.3/fabric>` or `26.3-fabric` instead of a version produced rows whose only possible outcome was
  a failed install of a jar that was already there.

## [0.3.4] - 2026-10-31

### Fixed

- **Updates now install while the game is running.** Minecraft keeps every jar in `mods/` open, so
  Windows refuses to replace one: the new build is written under its own file name and the jar it
  replaces is removed on the next launch, or deleted at once when Windows lets go of it. Nothing is
  ever written over a jar the game has open, which is the method Mod Menu Updater uses.
- **The list no longer offers a build that is already installed.** Two sources spell the same
  version their own way (`3.0.10+mc26.3` and `26.3-3.0.10`), and those rows tried to replace the open
  jar and failed. In the reported pack five of fourteen rows were of that kind.
- **A mod icon is also read from a root `icon.png`**, which CurseForge mods often ship, and a jar
  whose icon cannot be decoded now says why in the log instead of dropping to the initial tile
  silently.

## [0.3.3] - 2026-10-31

### Fixed

- **A mod that cannot be downloaded no longer cancels the whole install.** The other mods in the
  request are installed and the alert names the jar that failed, instead of losing every download
  because of one bad file. A missing required dependency still cancels the batch, which is what keeps
  a mod from being installed without the library it needs.
- **A failed install says why, on screen and in the log.** The reason names the file plus the HTTP
  status or the checksum mismatch, a download is retried once before giving up, and the task ends as a
  visible failure instead of leaving the screen on Installing forever.
